generations.prompt: Handheld electroshock stun device, 1980s police equipment. One boxy angular body like a rectangular brick, flat vertical sides, sharp edges, At the front end of the body sits a square dart cartridge, a separate block that is slightly narrower than the body, with two small round dart holes on its front face. Along both flat sides of the body, towards the front, is a large flat rectangular panel, slightly raised. Under the rear of the body hangs a thin straight vertical handle, narrow front to back and clearly separate from the body, with a small trigger and a square trigger guard at its front edge. No slide, no hammer, no barrel, no sights, no rail. Clean hard-surface industrial design, single object, no text, no logos, no hands, no stand.

Handheld electroshock stun gun for police, 1980s, L-shaped like a cordless drill or a staple gun in side view. The upper part is a long horizontal rectangular box, three times longer than it is tall, with flat sides and sharp angular edges. At the front end of that box is a smaller square cartridge block with two small round dart holes in its front face. On each flat side of the long box, in its front half, is a large flat rectangular plate. Hanging straight down from the rear half of the long box is a slim vertical handle, narrow front to back, with a small trigger and a square trigger guard at its front edge. No slide, no hammer, no barrel, no sights, no rail, no carry handle on top. Clean hard-surface industrial design, single object, no text, no logos, no hands, no stand.
